name: Somali Bariis Iskukaris
description: Bariis iskukaris, spiced rice cooked with meat and raisins, is one of Somalia's most beloved dishes, traditionally colored a warm orange-red with real xawaash spice blend.
steps_detailed: Brown the chicken with the onion, cumin, and cinnamon, 8-9 minutes.
Add the rice and 1.25 cups water, cover, and simmer 18-20 minutes until tender.
Stir in the raisins once cooked.

name: Somali Baasto
description: Baasto, spaghetti served with a spiced tomato-meat sauce and often a side of banana, reflects genuine Italian colonial influence merged with Somali spicing - eating pasta alongside a whole banana is a real, distinctive Somali custom, not an unusual pairing to skip.

steps_detailed: Brown the beef, 6-7 minutes.

name: Somali Suqaar
description: Suqaar, small cubes of meat sautéed with pepper and onion, a beloved Somali dish, often served over rice or with bread.
steps_detailed: Sear the beef over high heat, 4-5 minutes.
Add the onion, pepper, and jalapeño, and cook 5-6 minutes more.

name: Somali Canjeero
description: Canjeero, a spongy fermented flatbread similar to Ethiopian injera, is a Somali breakfast staple, traditionally torn and dipped in oil, sugar, or stew.
steps_detailed: Whisk the flour, vinegar, and 1 cup water into a thin batter.
Let sit at room temperature 6-8 hours to develop some tang.
Pour a thin layer into a hot, lightly oiled non-stick pan and cook, covered, without flipping, 2-3 minutes, until bubbles form and the edges lift.

name: Somali Sambusa
description: Sambusa, fried triangular pastries with a spiced meat filling, a beloved Somali snack especially during Ramadan.
steps_detailed: Brown the beef with the onion and cumin, 6-7 minutes.
Cut the phyllo into strips, fill, and fold into triangles.
Fry, turning, 3-4 minutes, until deeply golden.

name: Somali Muufo
description: Muufo, a simple cornmeal flatbread, a genuine Somali staple, especially common along the southern coast.
steps_detailed: Mix the cornmeal with water into a firm dough.
Flatten into a round and cook in a hot, dry pan, 4-5 minutes per side, until browned and cooked through.

name: Somali Hilib Ari (Grilled Meat)
description: Hilib ari, grilled meat, is central to Somali eating, traditionally goat, made here with beef, a widely available protein with a similarly hearty character.
steps_detailed: Rub the beef with the garlic and cumin.
Grill, turning, 12-15 minutes, until well charred and cooked through.

name: Somali Fish with Rice
description: Grilled or fried fish served with spiced rice, reflecting Somalia's long Indian Ocean coastline and fishing tradition.
steps_detailed: Cook the rice with the cumin per package directions.
Grill or pan-fry the fish, 4-5 minutes per side, until just cooked through.
Serve the fish over the rice.

name: Somali Xalwo
description: Xalwo (halwa), a dense, glossy, cardamom-scented sweet, is one of Somalia's most beloved treats, traditionally made for celebrations and Eid.
steps_detailed: Whisk the cornstarch with 0.75 cup water until smooth, then add the sugar and cardamom.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, 10-12 minutes, until thick and glossy.
Stir in the butter until melted and shiny.
